comments.author: @Me__Myself__and__I
comments.text:
THIS is the best and most accurate assessment of the current state of AI that I've seen recently.  People are saying progress has plateaued.  They are talking about and showing charts of the AI "hype" cycle going into the valley of dispare.  A shocking number of people who talk about this stuff clearly do not have a good picture/understanding of the situation.

But Wes gets it.  When Open AI released GPT 4 it shocked everyone and was way ahead of the competition.  OpenAI stated they were not going to start work on GPT5 for awhile.  Yet they have been very busy on tangential aspects: multi-modal, voice, image gen, video gen and figuring out how to optimize so that much smaller models could be nearly as good as their large flagship model.  All of that has been very impressive, they have been busy but none of that is a GPT5 next-gen model.  We haven't seen that, yet.  They have also been doing research and improving GPT4 to stay on top.  

Their competitors just recently caught up to GPT4, but OpenAI has had a year plus to pull ahead and get plans in place behind the scenes.  No one is talking about this.  Open AI very well may have been making inroads and signing contracts to position themselves in the next round while their competition was focused on playing catchup.

Once GPT5 is released, THEN and only then will we know if progress is plateauing or leaping ahead.  Anyone claiming progress is plateaued, the hype is over, the future isn't LLMs, etc is just completely full of s***.  All that massive investment in new AI training hardware is for next gen models and we haven't seen them yet.

comments.author: @Me__Myself__and__I
comments.text:
I just realized that the first true commercial use of video gen is very likely going to be music videos.  This is an existing commercial niche where they often try to push the boundaries and try new things.  Music videos have much more creative freedom than movies or TV.  As long as they look good, capyure attention and compliment the song they win, they don't necessarily have to be 100% accurate or perfect.  Plus they are short only being a few minutes which helps since current video models can only create shortish videos.

Seems to me this would be a perfect medium for existing perfessionals to use the technology to be more creative and try new things.  It would be a good proving ground for the models to be used seriously, get feedback and improve.  If they can progress to the point that many or most new music videos are created using generative AI then they will be in a better position for use in movies and TV.

Another stepping stone before movies and TV may be advertising/commercials.

How to Pronounce 'Simulator'
The word "simulator" is pronounced as /ˈsɪmjʊleɪtə(r)/. Here's a breakdown of the pronunciation:

"sim" sounds like "sim" in "simple"
"yu" sounds like the "u" in "dune" or "rue"
"lay" sounds like "lay" in "layer"
"ter" sounds like "ter" in "term"
So, it sounds like "sim-yu-lay-ter".
